item.title: MachStruct 2.2.0
item.description:
Large files and YAML. Files of 5 MB or more are now handled in full, and very large ones stay responsive. YAML files keep their comments when saved, and files with several documents open.

Added

  • YAML files with several --- documents open, such as Kubernetes manifests. Each document is an item of the root, and saving writes them back as separate documents.

Changed

  • Saving a YAML file keeps its comments. Value edits and key renames are written into the original text in place, so comments, anchors, quoting and blank lines survive. Adding, removing or moving entries still rewrites the whole file.
  • Containers with more than 1,000 children are shown in ranges such as [0 … 999]. A CSV file with 400,000 rows used to freeze the window for 20–30 seconds; it now opens in a few seconds.
  • Files that fail to open say what is wrong and where, with the line, the column and the offending line, for JSON, YAML and XML.
  • VoiceOver names every control, including the document tree, disclosure triangles, toolbar menus, the find and query fields, and table rows.

Fixed

  • Find & Replace and queries cover the whole of a large file. They used to see only rows that had been expanded.
  • Large files save and export in full. Unexpanded rows were exported as empty objects; edits to large CSV and YAML files can now be saved; deleting a key from a large JSON file survives saving; and edits are no longer lost while browsing.
  • Jumping to a search match in a large file showed the row without its values.

item.title: MachStruct 2.1.3
item.description:
A data-safety release. Updating is strongly recommended if you open CSV or YAML files: in earlier versions, saving one after an edit replaced its contents with JSON.

Fixed

  • Saving a CSV or YAML file replaced it with JSON. After any edit, ⌘S wrote the document as JSON into the original .csv or .yaml file, without warning. CSV and YAML files are now saved in their own format, and CSV keeps its delimiter and its header (or lack of one). XML files can't be saved after editing and are left untouched. Edits to CSV or YAML files of 5 MB or more can't be saved yet, and saving them reports an error instead of writing a partial file.
  • CSV rows with more fields than the header lost the extras. Surplus fields are now kept under generated column names (column_4, column_5, …) and are included when exporting as CSV.
  • YAML mappings with non-scalar keys lost those entries. A complex key such as ? [a, b] was skipped along with its value. Such keys are now shown as [a, b].

item.title: MachStruct 2.1.2
item.description:
A correctness release. Three of these fixes concern data MachStruct was displaying wrongly or writing back wrongly, so updating is recommended if you edit and save files.

Fixed

  • Large files could not be navigated. Expanding any object or array in a JSON file of 5 MB or more produced nothing — the arrow opened and no rows appeared. Files below 5 MB were unaffected, which is why it went unnoticed.
  • Saving a JSON file reordered its keys, dropped repeated keys, and rewrote its numbers. 8.7 was written back as 8.6999999999999993 and 1.0 as 1. The raw view showed the altered values before anything had been saved. Saving a file you have not edited now leaves it as it was.
  • Files containing very large whole numbers would not open at all — anything beyond 18,446,744,073,709,551,615, such as Twitter-style IDs. This worked in 2.1.0 and broke in 2.1.1.
  • The table view cut the first character off its leftmost column, so Order ID appeared as rder ID.
  • Search had no keyboard shortcut. ⌘F now focuses the search field, and Find… has been added to the Edit menu.

item.title: MachStruct 2.1.1
item.description:
Fixed

  • Object keys appeared in the wrong order, and repeated keys vanished, in files under 5 MB. Saving wrote back the truncated version. Structure now comes from the file’s bytes at every size, so a document reads the same whatever its size — and small files parse slightly faster.
  • Opening two documents at once could show one file’s data in the other, or hang the app. Search results, breadcrumbs and X-Ray schemas could report another document’s contents, and navigating to a search result could consume gigabytes of memory until the app was force-quit.
  • Whole-number decimals such as 1.0 were displayed and re-saved as 1, losing the number type and silently rewriting the file.
  • The download link on machstruct.com returned a 404 for some releases. Every release now publishes a versionless disk image.
